content:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has made his most explicit display of nuclear power in years, touring weapons facilities and inspecting an array of atomic warheads in photographs released by state media on Thursday, while declaring that his country's status as a nuclear-armed state is permanent and non-negotiable.

During an inspection on November 25 of a newly built weapons-grade nuclear materials production base, a nuclear-power equipment production base and the Nuclear Weapons Institute, Kim said North Korea was "systematically increasing the nuclear materials production capacity" to strengthen its arsenal, according to the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

"Our nuclear capability has now become a reality," KCNA quoted Kim as saying. "Denying this reality is just the recognition of failure." In a sharper warning, he added that any attempt to deny North Korea's nuclear status would be regarded as "an open declaration of war."

Kim also directed the nuclear weapons sector to focus on "utilising the tactical nukes of different missions in multiple domains" — a call, reported by [The Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/11/26/asia-pacific/north-korea-kim-tactical-nukes-us-japan/), to deploy smaller, battlefield-ready nuclear weapons across the army, navy and other branches of the armed forces.

The photographs released by KCNA, though deliberately blurred, were unusually revealing. Analysts identified metal casings of five separate warhead designs on display, including a "super-large" nuclear warhead that Pyongyang has repeatedly alluded to in recent years, as well as miniaturised tactical warheads of the Hwasan-31 type first shown in 2023. "This is the greatest number of nuclear warhead types we've seen in a single North Korean image," Ankit Panda, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, wrote in an analysis.

The images also appeared to show gas centrifuges used to enrich uranium, confirming that the tour included a working enrichment facility. That detail matters: only about a week earlier, Rafael Grossi, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency, warned that Pyongyang had been expanding its uranium-enrichment facilities to produce bomb-grade material, calling the trend a serious concern.

Perhaps the most striking disclosure was the visit to what KCNA called a "nuclear-powered equipment production base" — the first time Kim has been shown at such a facility, according to Seoul's unification ministry. Analysts said the equipment on display appeared to be for a naval nuclear reactor programme. Shin Jong-woo, secretary-general of the Korea Defence and Security Forum, said the facility was believed to be producing submarine reactors and parts, and that the pictured equipment could be used for a nuclear-powered submarine planned for 2027.

The tour was Kim's fourth visit to a nuclear facility since September 2024, following trips in September 2024, January 2025 and June this year — but the breadth of this one, covering material production, warhead design and naval propulsion in a single day, set it apart.

The numbers behind the display tell their own story. During US President Donald Trump's first term, North Korea produced only about six bombs' worth of fissile material a year, according to estimates from weapons experts. Today, experts say, the regime can produce about 12 to 15 bombs' worth annually — a doubling of capacity that matches Kim's claim of systematically expanding production. South Korea's defence minister said in August that Pyongyang was generally believed to possess between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads, an estimate drawn from private research organisations that Seoul could not officially confirm.

The timing of the show was pointed. It came days after a widely anticipated meeting between Trump and Kim failed to materialise during the US president's trip to Asia last week — a meeting Trump had publicly floated. Kim used the occasion for his most direct comments aimed at Washington since then, accusing the United States of approving South Korea's push to acquire a nuclear-powered submarine and of facilitating nuclear technology transfers within the alliance.

Kim's message, analysts say, is less about closing the door to talks than about setting the price of opening it. Panda wrote that the North Korean leader "is pretty clearly not interested in anything resembling denuclearization, but does appear to be interested in trying to get a fundamentally new bargain with the United States." In that reading, the warheads on display were not only weapons but bargaining chips — evidence that Pyongyang now negotiates, if it negotiates at all, as a recognised nuclear power rather than as a state seeking to trade its programme away.

That framing echoes the path Kim has taken since his last major diplomatic opening. The prospect of a meeting with Trump had raised hopes of renewed dialogue, a possibility that now looks remote: [earlier reporting on Trump's outreach](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/trump-may-meet-kim-jong-un-china-november-2026) noted that Pyongyang had left the overtures unanswered, and Thursday's display suggests the silence was deliberate.

North Korea has conducted six nuclear tests since 2006, the last and most powerful in 2017. Since then it has steadily built the infrastructure of a mature nuclear power: warheads small enough to fit on short-range missiles, a growing stockpile of fissile material, and now, apparently, the beginnings of a nuclear-powered navy. Kim's declaration that possession of nuclear weapons is his country's "irreversible option" and will remain so "forever in the future" leaves little room for doubt about where the programme goes next — outward, into new domains, and on a larger scale.
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear-material production and weapons research facilities on November 25, releasing rare photos of five warhead designs and calling for tactical nuclear weapons to be deployed across multiple domains, while declaring his country's nuclear status permanent and any denial of it an open declaration of war.
title: Kim Jong Un shows off five warhead designs and calls for tactical nuclear weapons across all domains
